title: Differentiation and characterization of human iPSC-derived vascular endothelial cells under physiological shear stress
protocol: Coat one 6-well plate with hESC-qualified Matrigel diluted 1:100 in DMEM/F-12 at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Remove a vial of iPSCs from liquid nitrogen and place it in a water bath set to 37°C.
Swirl the vial in the water until only a small ice chunk remains.
Transfer thawed cells to a 15 mL conical tube using a 1000 μl pipette.
Slowly add 9 mL warm mTeSR Plus to the cells using a serological pipette.
Centrifuge the cells at 170 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 4 mL warm mTeSR Plus with 10 μM ROCK inhibitor (Y-27632).
Plate cells in two wells of the Matrigel-coated 6-well plate by aspirating the Matrigel and adding 2 mL cell solution per well.
Shake the plate gently to evenly disperse cells.
Incubate the plate in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO₂ for 24 hours.
Replace media with 2 mL fresh mTeSR Plus without ROCK inhibitor per well the next day.
Feed cells with 2 mL warm mTeSR Plus per well every day for 2–3 more days until iPSC colonies are large enough to passage.
Passage the cells at a 1:1 ratio using EDTA if cells are not 60%–80% confluent within 4 days after thawing.
Aspirate Matrigel from the required number of Matrigel-coated wells and add 2 mL mTeSR Plus to each well for passage preparation.
Wash cells once with 1 mL PBS without calcium or magnesium per well.
Add 1 mL warm 0.5 mM EDTA to each well and leave at 20°C–25°C for 3 minutes.
Carefully aspirate the EDTA from the wells, not the cells.
Add 1 mL warm mTeSR Plus to each well of dissociated cells.
Scrape cells using a cell scraper.
Gently triturate using a 1000 μL pipette 4–6 times.
Combine the dissociated cells from both original wells and split among the new wells filled with mTeSR Plus.
Incubate in a humidified incubator at 37°C for 24 hours.
Feed the cells with 2 ml warm mTeSR Plus daily.
Passage the cells at low ratios (1:1 or 1:2) every 3 days until they achieve 60%-80% confluence within 3 days.
Repeat step 4 to passage cells at a 1:6 ratio in 6-well plates every 3 days for continued culture after recovery from thawing.
Fill 6 new wells with media when splitting 1 well of cells at a 1:6 ratio.
Add 160 μl dissociated cell solution to each of the new wells.
Coat one T-75 flask with hESC-qualified Matrigel diluted 1:100 in DMEM/F-12 at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Wash 60%–80% confluent iPSCs once with 1 mL PBS per well.
Aspirate PBS and add 1 mL Accutase to each well.
Incubate at 37°C for 3 minutes.
Lightly tap the plate to lift the iPSCs.
If they have not all detached, incubate the plate at 37°C for additional time in increments of 2 minutes until all cells have detached.
Total time in Accutase should not exceed 7 minutes.
Dilute Accutase 1:1 using warm mTeSR Plus.
Collect the cells from all wells into a 15 mL conical tube.
Count cells.
Centrifuge 3.5 million cells for one T-75 differentiation at 170 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 15 mL warm mTeSR Plus + 10 μM ROCK-Inhibitor.
Add cell suspension to the Matrigel-coated T-75 flask.
Prepare mesoderm induction media: Mix 50 mL warm N2B27 medium with 8 μM CHIR-99021 and 25 ng/mL hBMP4.
Aspirate mTeSR Plus from cells and add mesoderm induction media.
Incubate for 3 days without changing the media.
Prepare endothelial cell induction media: Mix 40 mL warm complete StemPro-34 medium with 200 ng/mL VEGF165 and 2 μM forskolin.
Change media to fresh 40 mL endothelial cell induction media every day on days 4, 5, and 6.
Collect conditioned media from differentiating endothelial cells on days 5, 6, and 7 for later use.
Prepare 50 mL chilled MACS buffer and keep it on ice in the cell culture hood.
Coat 20 collagen-coated T-75 flasks with 0.05 mg/mL Collagen I in 0.02 N Acetic Acid at 20°C–25°C for 1 hour, then rinse with PBS.
Collect day 7 conditioned media from cells and wash with 10 mL PBS.
Add 5 mL Accutase and incubate at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Add 5 mL cold StemPro-34 and transfer cells to a 50 mL conical tube.
Count cells.
Centrifuge at 170 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate supernatant and wash cells with 10 mL cold MACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 170 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend cells in 8 μL cold MACS buffer per million cells.
Add 2 μl per million cells of Fc Blocking Buffer.
Mix well by pipetting after adding each component.
Incubate cells on ice for 15 minutes.
While the cells are incubating, combine conditioned media collected from days 5, 6, and 7 (total 120 mL).
Add an equal volume (120 mL) of fresh complete StemPro-34 medium supplemented with heparin (2 μg/ml) and Pen/Strep.
Filter the combined media through a 0.22 μm vacuum filter.
Warm filtered conditioned media to 37°C in a water bath.
After the 15-minute incubation, wash labeled cells by adding 1 mL cold MACS buffer per million cells (maximum of 30 mL if cell yield is greater than 30 million).
Centrifuge at 170 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 mL cold MACS buffer.
Prepare LS column and magnet on a MACS stand in the cell culture hood.
Obtain three 50 mL conical tubes and one 15 mL conical tube for sorting and place them in the hood.
Add 1 mL cold MACS buffer to the LS column.
Collect the flow-through in the first 50 mL conical tube and discard.
Move immediately to step 10t after completing the flowing process.
Add the cell suspension to the LS column.
Collect the flow-through in the second 50 mL conical tube.
Collect the flow-through from the previous step and reapply to the top of the column.
Collect the flow-through in the third 50 mL conical tube.
Add 500 μL MACS buffer to the LS column.
Continue to collect the flow-through in the third 50 mL conical tube.
Repeat washing two more times with 500 μL MACS buffer to remove remaining negative cells from the column.
Remove LS column from the magnet and place it in a prepared 15 mL conical tube.
Add 1 mL PBS to the column and use the plunger to release the cells into the conical tube.
Add 4 mL PBS to the retrieved positive fraction of cells.
Count the cells using an appropriate method.
Centrifuge the cells at 170 × g for 5 minutes.
Plate 26,000 cells per square centimeter in collagen-coated T-75 flasks with approximately 2 million cells per flask and 20 mL warm complete conditioned media.
Replace the media with 10 mL every other day until the conditioned media is depleted or until the first passage.
Feed viECs with 10 mL warm viEC media every other day.
Culture viECs in viEC media when conditioned media is depleted, following the first passage, or the day before cryopreserving p0 viECs.
Cryopreserve viECs at 90% confluence (1 million cells per vial in 1 mL CryoSFM freezing medium) and store in liquid nitrogen.
Passage viECs when they reach 90% confluence.
Coat the culture vessel with 0.05 mg/mL Collagen I diluted in 0.02 N Acetic Acid at 20°C–25°C for 1 hour, then wash once with PBS.
Add 5 mL Accutase to viECs.
Incubate at 37°C for 2–3 minutes.
Lightly tap the plate to detach the cells.
Dilute Accutase with 5 mL warm viEC media.
Collect the cells in a conical tube and count cells.
Centrifuge cells at 170 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend cells in viEC media.
Plate 15,000–25,000 viECs/cm².
Feed 24 hours after passaging.
Feed every other day until the next passage.
Freeze 1 million cells per cryovial in 1 mL CryoSFM freezing medium for cryopreservation.
Thaw into warm viEC media then plate on collagen coated plates (1 million cells per T-75) to thaw cryopreserved viECs.
Feed the day after thawing, then every other day.
Supplement with 10 μM TGFβ inhibitor SB431542 when feeding viECs for improved proliferation.
Coat Nunc polystyrene SlideFlasks with 0.05 mg/mL Collagen I in 0.02 M Acetic Acid for 1 hour.
Wash the coated flasks once with PBS.
Passage viECs to slides at a density of 27,000 viECs/cm² (∼250,000 viECs per 9 cm² SlideFlask) using Accutase in 4 mL of viEC media per SlideFlask.
Feed the cells the day after passaging.
Feed the cells every other day thereafter.
Set up parallel plate flow experiment for viEC behavior under physiological shear stress.
Assemble and sterilize the flow circuit components.
Obtain and autoclave two fine-point tweezers.
Warm 37 mL viEC media in a 37°C water bath.
Assemble the pulse dampener by obtaining two sterile 4-way stopcocks linked in series.
Screw two sterile 60 mL Luer-Lock syringes into the top outlet of each stopcock.
Pull the plunger for each syringe up to the 25 mL mark.
Attach the female luer + 3/32″ barb fitting on the inlet tubing to the left side of the pulse dampener.
Attach the male luer + 3/32″ barb fitting on outlet tubing to the right side.
Connect a 0.22 μm syringe filter to the female luer + 3/32″ barbed fitting of the gas exchange tubing.
Secure the connection with parafilm.
Tape the syringes to a conical tube holder, perpendicular to the flat surface of the biosafety cabinet.
Fill the reservoir bottle with 30 mL warm viEC media and screw the cap closed.
Reinforce any loose autoclave tape on the cap with lab tape.
Secure the media reservoir bottle and pulse dampener conical rack to a tray using lab tape.
Attach the inlet tubing to the pump.
Fill the inlet tubing by turning on the pump at a speed of 9 mL/min.
Stop the pump when media can be seen flowing through the stopcocks of the pulse dampener.
Fill the first syringe in the pulse dampener with 5 mL of media using stopcocks to block flow past the first syringe and allow flow into it.
Turn the left stopcock so that the OFF switch is pointed to the right, blocking flow past the first syringe.
Turn the second stopcock so that the OFF switch is pointed up, blocking flow into the second syringe.
Use the pump set to 9 mL/min until the media level reaches 5 mL inside the first syringe.
Turn off the pump once the syringe contains 5 mL of media.
Fill the second syringe in the pulse dampener with 5 mL of media.
Use the left stopcock to block media flow into the first syringe by turning it so that the OFF switch is pointed up.
Use the right stopcock to block media flow past the second syringe by turning it so that the OFF switch is pointed right.
Turn on the pump until the media level reaches 5 mL inside the second syringe, then turn it off.
Secure the plunger of both syringes at the 30 mL mark using parafilm.
Secure plungers well with parafilm.
Mark the location of each plunger’s end on each syringe around the 30 mL mark with a lab marker.
Turn both stopcocks so that the OFF switches are pointed down, allowing media to flow in all directions through tubing and syringes.
Fill the rest of the tubing until media drips out of the outlet tubing back into the reservoir bottle.
Shake the tubing to move air bubbles out through the outlet.
Ensure that no air bubbles remain in the tubing.
Slowly turn up the pump to 52 mL/min in increments of ∼15 mL/min.
Ensure that the pulse dampener plungers do not move and the flow circuit is stable.
Allow the pump to continue running at this speed as a test while you assemble the flow chamber.
Lay the bottom of the flow chamber flat on the biosafety cabinet surface or a sterile tray.
Use sterile tweezers to secure the gasket onto the screws at a slightly elevated position from the bottom of the chamber.
Retrieve the SlideFlask of confluent viECs from the incubator.
Spray the SlideFlask with 70% ethanol.
Dry the SlideFlask with a Kim wipe.
Place the SlideFlask on a sterile surface in the cell culture hood.
Aspirate the media from the flask.
Use a SlideFlask removal tool to remove the culture chamber from the slide.
Wedge the tool underneath the lip of the flask and use it as a lever to crack the flask off the slide.
Keep pressure on the forceps to keep the slide flat and pull the flask completely off the slide with your other hand.
Transfer the slide to its designated groove in the bottom piece of flow chamber using sterile tweezers.
Use both pairs of sterile tweezers to bring the gasket down, making it flush with the bottom of the chamber.
Add 7 mL warm viEC media on top of the slide using a 5 mL serological pipette.
Line up the top chamber piece with the screws of the bottom and bring it halfway down to the surface of the cells.
Release the top chamber piece quickly from your fingers to allow it to fall into place.
Drop the top of the chamber onto the cells rather than lowering it slowly.
Practice the dropping step without cells using only water or media before performing the full experiment.
Secure the two halves of the flow chamber by screwing in the wingnuts starting from the corners and moving to the middle.
Screw in diagonally opposite wingnuts such that pressure remains even on both sides of the chamber.
Tighten the wingnuts as much as possible using pliers without breaking the acrylic.
Wipe off any spilled media from the flow chamber using Kim wipes soaked in 70% ethanol.
Turn the pump off.
Connect the outlet tubing to one of the flow chamber ports.
Disconnect the outlet tubing from the 5/32″ straight tubing connector between two short stretches of L/S 16 tubing.
Connect one end of the L/S 16 tubing to the other side of the flow chamber.
Optional: Wrap a small piece of parafilm around the connection site to prevent leaking.
Place the flow chamber on the tray with the pulse dampener and media reservoir.
Turn the pump down to 9 mL/min and turn it on.
Allow the media to flow through the flow chamber and drip into the reservoir for a few seconds.
Turn the pump down to 9 mL/min before flowing over the cells.
Disconnect the tubing from the pump.
Transfer the tray with the flow circuit to a cell culture incubator.
Place the pump on top of the cell culture incubator.
Connect the inlet tubing to the pump and secure it to the incubator.
Turn on the pump and close the incubator door.
Maintain the flow at 9 mL/min for 15 minutes.
Increase the pump flow rate to 18 mL/min and maintain this rate for 45 minutes.
Increase the pump flow rate to 36 mL/min and maintain this rate for 1 hour.
Turn the pump flow rate up to 52 mL/min.
Maintain this flow rate for 24 hours.
Turn the pump off after 24 hours.
Disconnect the tubing from the pump and move the flow circuit tray to the biosafety cabinet.
Use a 5/32″ straight tubing connector to link the open ends of the disconnected tubing.
Unscrew each wingnut, starting from the corners and moving towards the middle in diagonally opposite pairs.
Remove all the wingnuts completely.
Lift the top half of the flow chamber off the bottom half to expose the cells.
Use tweezers to carefully remove the gasket.
Transfer the slide with cells into a petri dish filled with warm viEC media using tweezers.
Note the flow direction for future reference if planning on imaging the slide.
Rinse the flow chamber with water.
Scrub the flow chamber with Alconox.
Dry the flow chamber completely.
EtO sterilize the flow chamber.
Autoclave wingnuts.
Fill the media reservoir with bleach and leave for 15 minutes.
Rinse the media reservoir with dH2O.
Allow the media reservoir to dry on a drying rack.
Flush the tubing with 70% ethanol.
Flush the tubing with dH2O.
Flush the tubing with air.
Hang the tubing and allow it to air-dry completely.
Reassemble the tubing and reservoir.
Sterilize by autoclaving or EtO sterilization.
Discard the 60 mL syringes.
Flush the 4-way stopcocks with ethanol.
Allow the stopcocks to dry.
EtO sterilize the stopcocks.
Aspirate viEC media from the slide placed in a petri dish with warm viEC media.
Wash the slide with PBS twice.
Add 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) to cover the slide.
Incubate cells with PFA at 20°C–25°C for 15 minutes.
Aspirate PFA and wash cells with PBS three times for 5 minutes each.
Use tweezers to pick up the slide.
Dab the bottom of the slide lightly with a Kim wipe to remove excess PBS.
Place the slide on a dry, flat, clean surface.
Add 220 μl lysis buffer to the culture area until it fills the area with cells.
Scrape the lysis buffer and cells off the slide into one well of a 6-well plate.
Repeat steps for all slides if processing multiple at once.
Include a static control for each flow slide.
Proceed with RNA extraction according to the specific kit protocol.
Pause Point: Isolated RNA can be stored at −80°C for up to 1 year.
Prepare 5 mM DAF-FM DA by dissolving 50 μg DAF-FM DA in 20 μL DMSO.
Dissolved DAF-FM DA stock can be stored at −20°C for up to 6 months.
Warm serum-free viEC media with complete StemPro-64, 50 μg/ml VEGF, and 2 μg/ml heparin to 37°C.
Add 1 μM DAF-FM DA to warm serum-free viEC media.
Aspirate the media from slides and add serum-free viEC media with DAF-FM DA.
Incubate viECs with DAF-FM DA for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Aspirate media containing DAF-FM DA and rinse cells once with PBS.
Aspirate PBS and add fresh warm serum-free viEC media.
Incubate viECs for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Image viECs immediately at 10× magnification.
Quantify DAF-FM DA-positive viECs per unit area using image analysis software.
